results.title: Meta4XNLI: A Cross-lingual Parallel Corpus for Metaphor Detection and Interpretation
results.content: In this work, we present Meta4XNLI, the first parallel dataset for Natural Language Inference (NLI) newly annotated for metaphor detection and interpretation in both English and Spanish. For metaphor detection, we trained models in other datasets and evaluated them cross-domain in Meta4XNLI; we fine-tuned and evaluated Masked Language Models (MLM, encoders only) and decoders-only Large Language Models (LLMs) with Meta4XNLI for both languages and also in zero-shot scenarios. Similarly, Berger (2022) explores transfer learning techniques, such as neural machine translation, cross-lingual word embeddings, or multilingual pre-trained language models, to obtain a dataset for metaphor detection in German from English corpora. Table 1: Available datasets for metaphor detection and interpretation according to their features; task: det for detection, paraphr for paraphrase; Level: Annotation level, namely, sentence or token level; NL: spontaneous language, in opposition to sentences with a fixed structure or generated through lexical substitution; : corpus structured in sentence pairs, usually hypothesis and premise in NLI. The outcome of this annotation process is Meta4XNLI, the first parallel dataset with labels for the tasks of metaphor detection and interpretation via NLI in ES and EN. Table 11: Monolingual metaphor detection encoder-only models: F1 score results from model fine-tuning with Meta4XNLI (M4X) and evaluation with its test set language and VUAM (EN) and CoMeta (ES) test sets, for each corresponding language. Table 12: Monolingual metaphor detection decoder-only models: F1 score results from model fine-tuning with Meta4XNLI (M4X) and evaluation with its test set language and VUAM (EN) and CoMeta (ES) test sets, for each corresponding language. Table 13: Multilingual metaphor detection: Results from models fine-tuned with Meta4XNLIES + Meta4XNLIEN and evaluated on each language test set individually. In this work, we present Meta4XNLI, the first cross-lingual parallel dataset in ES and EN labeled for metaphor detection and interpretation framed within the task of NLI. The key steps implemented in this project are as follows: * **Conversion of Metaphor IDs to Metaphor Words:** Replacing metaphor IDs with corresponding metaphor words to establish a direct link between textual instances and specific metaphors. * **Feature Engineering:** Truncating text to a single sentence containing the metaphor word to enhance the model's focus on the immediate context of the metaphor. * **BERT-Based Sequence Classifier:** Utilizing a pre-trained BERT model for sequence classification, leveraging BERT's contextual embeddings to discern subtle nuances in language usage. * **Key Features of BERT:** Bidirectional context processing, state-of-the-art natural language processing model with multiple layers of self-attention mechanisms. 3. Significance of the Dataset * The dataset used in this project is meticulously crafted and labeled, facilitating robust metaphor detection model training and exploration of metaphor usage intricacies in natural language. * Clear differentiation between literal and metaphorical instances enables the model to discern nuanced language patterns and make informed predictions. * Two distinct methodologies are explored, leveraging advanced natural language processing techniques and deep learning models for effective metaphor detection. * Precision is highlighted as a crucial metric in assessing the model's reliability in correctly classifying metaphorical instances. This project contributes to advancing the field of natural language processing by addressing the challenges posed by metaphorical language and providing a valuable tool for understanding and analyzing textual content. Metaphor detection with NLP identifies figurative language in text. It assigns metaphor IDs to words, labels their metaphorical usage, and analyzes texts to determine metaphorical functions.

results.title: Mastering Metaphor Detection Techniques - Number Analytics
results.content: Rule-Based Approaches to Metaphor Detection Rule-based approaches to metaphor detection rely on predefined linguistic patterns and rules to identify metaphors in text. By identifying these patterns, researchers can develop rules to detect metaphors. Some common linguistic patterns used in rule-based approaches include: * Verb-noun combinations: Identifying unusual verb-noun combinations can help detect metaphors. To overcome these limitations, researchers have turned to machine learning and deep learning approaches, which can learn to detect metaphors from large datasets. These models can learn to detect metaphors by identifying the features and patterns that are associated with metaphorical language use. ### Feature Extraction and Representation Feature extraction and representation are critical components of machine learning and deep learning approaches to metaphor detection. Some common features used in metaphor detection include: * Word embeddings: Word embeddings like Word2Vec 4 and GloVe 5 provide a dense representation of words that can capture their semantic relationships. These architectures can learn to detect metaphors by identifying complex patterns and features in text data. Some common deep learning architectures used for metaphor detection include: * Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs): CNNs can be used to extract local features from text data that are indicative of metaphors. Some common evaluation methods used for metaphor detection include: * Cross-validation: Cross-validation involves evaluating a model on multiple folds of a dataset to ensure its robustness. The following diagram illustrates a simple stacking architecture for metaphor detection: A["Text Input"] --> B["Rule-Based Model"]; A --> C["Machine Learning Model"]; By integrating multiple approaches, researchers can develop more accurate and robust metaphor detection systems that can handle a wide range of linguistic and cultural variations. Metaphor detection is a challenging task that requires a deep understanding of linguistic structures, semantic relationships, and cultural variations. By leveraging rule-based approaches, machine learning, and deep learning techniques, researchers can develop accurate and effective metaphor detection systems. ### Q: What are some common approaches to metaphor detection? A: Common approaches to metaphor detection include rule-based approaches, machine learning, and deep learning techniques. A: Metaphor detection systems can be improved by handling errors and ambiguities, incorporating cultural and linguistic knowledge, and integrating multiple approaches.

results.title: Applying Additional Auxiliary Context Using Large Language Model for Metaphor Detection
results.content: Comparing results between VUA\_All and VUA\_Verb can reveal whether metaphor detection models benefit from context depending on the grammatical category of the target word. We evaluated the impact of adding prior context on metaphor detection across three datasets: MOH-X, VUA\_All, and VUA\_Verb. In the MOH-X dataset (Table 11), the addition of 5-word following context using P1\_5words achieved the highest accuracy (0.8469), precision (0.8455), and F1 score (0.8429). For the VUA\_Verb dataset (Table 13), which focuses on verb metaphors, P1\_10words reached the highest accuracy (0.8718) and F1 score (0.7569) on the validation set. This section synthesizes findings from the main experiments, ablation studies, and error analyses, to evaluate how auxiliary context affects metaphor detection across MOH-X, VUA\_All, and VUA\_Verb. The most significant gains were observed in MOH-X, a dataset composed of short, metaphor-dense sentences, where prior context achieved an F1 score of 0.8493 and precision of 0.8601. Table A7 shows the F1 scores across three datasets (MOH-X, VUA\_All, VUA\_Verb) under different context settings (Prior, Prior+Following).
